brief: Add a third storey to this caddy without moving or removing anything that is already on it.

requirements.requirement: Add a third storey to the caddy
requirements.evidence: New tower at cell 1,1: piece:1,1,0;full, piece:1,1,1;full, piece:1,1,2;full with bin:1,1,2~hex-bin-full-div3 on the level-2 (third storey) base, joined to the caddy by connector:0#1,0|1,1. The original column 0,0 could not be raised directly: the configurator refused a level-2 base there with BIN_RIM_IN_JOINT because the existing level-1 bin's rim stands in the stacking joint (a binned cell is the top of its column), so the third storey sits on an adjacent new column instead of directly over the existing top.

requirements.requirement: Do not move or remove anything already on the caddy
requirements.evidence: All 20 original nodes are still present and unchanged (handles, hook, bins bin:-1,0,0 / bin:1,0,0 / bin:0,0,1~hex-bin-full-div3-x2, notches, caps, joint bolts, fused and pieces at 0,0 levels 0-1); a riser briefly placed on 0,0,1 was undone, and every addition went into new cells (1,1 levels 0-2).

requirements.requirement: House rules and verification (cap open faces, lock joints, check_build)
requirements.evidence: capOpenFaces added solid caps on the new column's open faces, lockJoints ran, and check_build returned ok with meshClash clear and no issues.

finish.summary: Added a third storey without touching the existing caddy: a new adjacent column at cell 1,1 (bases at levels 0, 1 and 2) carries a full-depth 3-compartment bin on its level-2 base, side-connected to the original caddy at ground level. The original top cell (0,0) could not be stacked on directly — the configurator refuses a base over its existing bin (BIN_RIM_IN_JOINT: a binned cell is the top of its column) and the brief forbade removing it — so the raised storey is beside, not above, the old top. All original parts, bins, handles, hook and notches remain in place; caps and joint locking applied to the new work; check_build is clear.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
cuts: buy 1 x 10 ft 3/4 in Sch 40 PVC pipe, OD 26.67 mm (US). Metric 25/32 mm pipe does not fit.
- fit a BACKFLOW PREVENTER at the hose bib: this system is a cross-connection without one
- fit a 25-40 psi PRESSURE REGULATOR at the inlet
- drain the system before it freezes
